observations: body L1-L3: al-Battānī adds the minutes of the first parallax to the place and the anomaly of the Moon (translation, p. 104, l. 24–27); the argument of latitude is corrected only at the end, with the equated hours (p. 105, l. 38–42). On the figure of p. 277, L′L² measures 51.5 pt and S′σ′ 49.8 pt.
body L4: the superscript 2 of the second «λ²», after «supputetur;», prints with its foot faint, like a question mark.
body L10, L18, L30-L31: «al–Battānī» is letter-spaced, with long dashes (5.4, 5.4 and 5.3 pt); «Albatenii» (L31) is letter-spaced.

body L15-L25, L30-L31: the statement of al-Battānī that Schiaparelli rejects holds. ε² is the second parallax divided by the relative hourly motion (L10-L11; translation, p. 104, l. 29–30), so that in the time ε² the Moon gains on the Sun exactly the second parallax, and at ϑ + ε² the true longitudes of the Moon and the Sun differ by the second parallax; Schiaparelli's own reason in L15-L17 rests on this. The difference Δ of the apparent longitudes at ϑ + ε² is therefore the difference of the second and the third parallax, whether it is null or not, and al-Battānī's rule, which divides the excess of the third parallax over the second, or its defect, by the motus aequatus (p. 105, l. 23–37), divides Δ itself. Schiaparelli's remark in L23-L25 is right about the inference it names, but al-Battānī's equality does not rest on that inference. Both assume, as the whole method does, a uniform relative motion over the interval.

body L18-L19: the places cited are those printed in italics in the translation: p. 104, l. 41–42, p. 105, l. 1–3, 24–25 and 34, and p. 110, l. 25–26. The dashes of «41–» and «–42», divided between the lines, measure 5.4 and 5.3 pt, those of «1–3» and «24–25» 5.3 and 5.4 pt.
body L23, L30, L44: the dashes measure 9.6, 10.1 and 10.2 pt; in L44 the dash follows «respondens.» without a space (0.7 pt).

body L35, L37, L45: a speck stands before «consideratam» (L35); specks stand after «parallaxes» (L37), one on the baseline like a stop, though the sentence runs on; the c of «necessario» (L45) prints broken, in two specks.
